assessed_skill: Enumerate the complete set of routine screening schedules permitted by the specified guideline.

clinical_scope.population: A 58-year-old asymptomatic US woman at average risk who has undergone annual mammography, is in good health, has a life expectancy of at least 10 more years, and wishes to continue screening.

source_rights.attribution: 病例、雙語題文、選項、詳解與評分準則由 Medical Benchmark Collection 自編。篩檢間隔與適用條件依據美國癌症協會公開指引。
source_rights.scope: 本批僅將專案原創題文用於公開開發。ACS 著作另依原站內容使用政策處理，證據保留書目、定位與指紋。

review.question_for_reviewer: 請核對在此病例條件與 ACS 指引下，完整集合是否僅含每年及每兩年一次，兩種語言是否同樣要求列全。

variants.question: 美國一家診所依美國癌症協會（ACS）的指引，檢視例行乳房攝影篩檢的提醒設定（查核日為 2026 年 11 月 26 日）。病例是一名 58 歲女性，沒有乳房症狀，乳癌風險一般。她從 45 歲起每年接受篩檢，這次結果正常。她健康狀況良好，預期餘命至少還有 10 年，並希望繼續接受例行篩檢。請選出選項中所有符合 ACS 建議、診所可以設定的篩檢間隔，並說明依據。
variants.rationale: 依 ACS 對這個年齡層的建議，她可以改為每兩年一次，也可以繼續原本每年一次的篩檢。她的健康狀況與預期餘命符合繼續篩檢的條件。每三年一次及每六個月一次都不在這項例行建議所列的週期內。

clinical_update.question: 美國一家診所依美國癌症協會（ACS）的指引，檢視例行乳房攝影篩檢的提醒設定（查核日為 2026 年 11 月 26 日）。病例是一名 58 歲女性，沒有乳房症狀，乳癌風險一般。她從 45 歲起每年接受篩檢，這次結果正常。她健康狀況良好，預期餘命至少還有 10 年，並希望繼續接受例行篩檢。請選出選項中所有符合 ACS 建議、診所可以設定的篩檢間隔，並說明依據。
clinical_update.rationale: 依 ACS 對這個年齡層的建議，她可以改為每兩年一次，也可以繼續原本每年一次的篩檢。她的健康狀況與預期餘命符合繼續篩檢的條件。每三年一次及每六個月一次都不在這項例行建議所列的週期內。
rubric: 選出 A 與 D，順序不限，不加入 B 或 C。
說明她可以改為每兩年一次或維持每年一次，並依病例的健康狀況與預期餘命解釋持續篩檢的適用性。

claims.text: 這名 58 歲女性屬一般風險且健康狀況良好，預期餘命至少 10 年，符合 ACS 所列繼續例行篩檢的條件。
年滿 55 歲且原本每年篩檢者可改採每兩年一次，也可繼續每年一次；本題的兩個相符選項為 A 與 D。

variants.question: A US clinic is reviewing its routine screening mammography reminder policy using American Cancer Society (ACS) guidance current on November 26, 2026. The example is an asymptomatic 58-year-old woman at average risk of breast cancer. She has had yearly mammograms since age 45, and her latest screen was normal. She is in good health, has a life expectancy of at least 10 more years, and wishes to continue routine screening. Select every listed interval that the clinic could use under ACS guidance and explain your reasoning.
variants.rationale: Under the ACS guidance for her age group, she may switch to screening every two years or stay on her annual schedule. Her health and life expectancy support continued screening. The listed routine schedules do not include three-year or six-month intervals.

clinical_update.question: A US clinic is reviewing its routine screening mammography reminder policy using American Cancer Society (ACS) guidance current on November 26, 2026. The example is an asymptomatic 58-year-old woman at average risk of breast cancer. She has had yearly mammograms since age 45, and her latest screen was normal. She is in good health, has a life expectancy of at least 10 more years, and wishes to continue routine screening. Select every listed interval that the clinic could use under ACS guidance and explain your reasoning.
clinical_update.rationale: Under the ACS guidance for her age group, she may switch to screening every two years or stay on her annual schedule. Her health and life expectancy support continued screening. The listed routine schedules do not include three-year or six-month intervals.
rubric: Select A and D in either order and omit B and C.
Explain the option to switch to a two-year interval or continue annually, and relate continued screening to her health and life expectancy.

claims.text: This average-risk woman is 58, in good health, and expected to live at least another 10 years, meeting the ACS conditions for ongoing routine screening.
For this woman already on an annual schedule, ACS permits a switch to screening every other year or continuation of yearly screening. Those intervals correspond to A and D.

evidence.title: American Cancer Society Recommendations for the Early Detection of Breast Cancer
evidence.version: ACS public guidance revised 2026-07-23 and checked 2026-11-26. See also its guideline panel’s 2015 recommendation 1b, DOI 10.1001/jama.2015.12783.
evidence.locator: American Cancer Society screening recommendations → Guidelines for women at average breast cancer risk. The first list defines average risk. In the second list, bullet 3 covers both screening intervals for ages 55 and older and the health and life-expectancy conditions for continuing screening.
